name: Kestrel Field - autonomous operations showcase
description: Synthetic Permian-style oil field (96 ESP wells, 12 pads, 3 tank batteries, 2 compressor stations, gas plant, LACT terminal, 3 SWD wells, 8 trucks, 2 workover rigs). Two identical copies of the field run side by side from the same state with the same events: one operated by PLYXIS, one by typical manual operations.

events.title: Compressor unit trip at CS-1
events.narrative: One of three compressor units at CS-1 trips. Compression capacity drops by a third while the field keeps sending gas.

events.title: ESP on PAD-11 W-01 starts degrading fast
events.narrative: Bearing wear accelerates on a high-rate pump. Only vibration telemetry reveals it.

events.title: Injectivity loss at SWD-2
events.narrative: Formation plugging cuts the injection capacity of SWD-2 by more than half. Nothing announces it - the twin has to notice.

events.name: gas_price
events.title: Pipeline maintenance notice: Waha gas turns negative
events.narrative: A midstream maintenance notice pushes the Waha hub price to -2.50 USD/Mscf for 24 hours starting in 4 hours.

events.name: gas_price
events.title: Negative gas price in effect
events.narrative: Every Mscf sold now costs money.

events.title: New well tied in on PAD-07
events.narrative: A new well is brought online by the completions team. It is not in any engineering database yet - only its SCADA tags appear.

events.title: Compressor unit trip at CS-2
events.narrative: Second compression event during the negative-price window.

demo.title: One operating system for the whole field
demo.text: Kestrel Field: 96 wells, 3 tank batteries, 2 compressor stations, trucks, rigs. Left: what PLYXIS operates. The same field is also run by conventional manual operations in parallel - same starting point, same events, same physics.

demo.title: The digital twin is the map
demo.text: Every asset on the map is an instance of a PLX blueprint, instantiated from the asset register by about 120 lines of field code. Flows, tank levels and trucks are live.

demo.title: Disruption: compressor trip
demo.text: A CS-1 unit trips. PLYXIS detects the status change, re-plans the whole field and pushes new set points within seconds - shifting gas to CS-2 and easing the gassiest wells instead of flaring, while a lease crew is dispatched to restart the unit.

demo.title: Why did it do that?
demo.text: Every decision carries its reasons: marginal oil value, power cost and the shadow price of the binding bottleneck - computed from the model, not generated text.

demo.title: Predictive maintenance
demo.text: Vibration on PAD-11 W-01 is trending up. The twin infers the falling pump health that no sensor measures, extrapolates the time to alarm and plans a workover rig for a replacement before the pump fails.

demo.title: Reality drifts - the twin follows
demo.text: SWD-2 lost more than half of its injectivity and nobody told the system. The injection pressure no longer matched the twin, so the estimator re-estimated the disposal capacity within hours; the planner re-routed water and eased the wells with the most water per barrel of oil.

demo.title: Markets move - operations follow
demo.text: Waha gas is negative for 24 hours. PLYXIS re-prices every barrel: oil still pays for the gas it brings, so it keeps producing - and it does not flare to dodge the price, which would cost carbon and break the zero-routine-flaring policy.

demo.title: The twin rewrites itself
demo.text: Unknown tags from a new well appeared. A discovery rule turned them into PLX code - reviewed, committed and compiled into the live twin in seconds.

demo.title: Value
demo.text: Same field, same events: the difference in production, profit, flaring and emissions is the value of autonomous operations.
